abstention.statement: While EGFL8 has strong genetic association to psoriasis (e.g. GWAS rs3117182) and an Open Targets score for the disease, there is no mechanistic evidence linking it to the IL-23/Th17 axis or demonstrating how it contributes to psoriasis, nor are there any ChEMBL compounds targeting it. GLE1 and UHRF2 lack even a genetic association to psoriasis and have no relevant drug targets. There is insufficient functional evidence to build falsifiable mechanisms for these three genes.
abstention.what_would_change_this: Functional studies demonstrating how EGFL8 variation alters skin biology or the IL-23/IL-17 axis, and genome-wide association hits or validated therapeutic compounds for GLE1 and UHRF2 in psoriasis.

hypotheses.mechanism: IL12B encodes the p40 subunit of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-23. IL-23 directly binds to its extracellular receptor, IL23R, which is expressed on naive and memory T cells. This binding event acts as the primary signal triggering T-helper 17 (Th17) cell lineage commitment and expansion, which is the central pathogenic driver of psoriatic skin inflammation.
hypotheses.title: IL12B and IL23R drive psoriasis via extracellular IL-23 signaling

object.label: positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

subject.label: positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

falsification.description: Administering a selective TYK2 inhibitor in an IL-23-induced skin inflammation model to test if JAK-STAT signaling and psoriatic phenotypes are significantly reduced compared to vehicle.

readout.label: positive regulation of receptor signaling pathway via JAK-STAT

hypotheses.mechanism: Upon engagement of the IL-23 receptor, the intracellular Janus kinase TYK2 is activated. TYK2 mediates the positive regulation of the JAK-STAT signaling pathway by phosphorylating downstream STAT proteins. This intracellular signaling cascade is strictly required to translate the IL-23 signal into the Th17-mediated inflammatory response that produces psoriasis.
hypotheses.title: TYK2 mediates intracellular signaling from the IL-23 receptor to drive psoriasis

falsification.description: Knocking out TRAF3IP2 in a human keratinocyte cell line and measuring whether the application of exogenous IL-17 can still induce psoriatic inflammatory marker expression.

hypotheses.mechanism: The Th17 cells expanded by the IL-23 axis secrete interleukin-17, which acts on target cells like keratinocytes. TRAF3IP2 (Act1) is an essential intracellular adaptor protein that links the activated IL-17 receptor to downstream inflammatory signaling. Genetic variants in TRAF3IP2 alter this terminal signaling step, directly increasing the risk of developing psoriasis.
hypotheses.title: TRAF3IP2 mediates downstream IL-17 receptor signaling in psoriasis
